candidates.basis: exact_source_inventory events=['Frontend Collision or Rear-end Collision or Collision with Pedestrian detected']; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions transition:line:22 triggers=[merged event], guard=null; fcstm_model.model_ir.events single event entry; NL2 quote.
candidates.expected: NL requires the sub-machine activation to be triggered by exactly one of three named, distinguishable detection conditions (frontend collision, rear-end collision, pedestrian collision), implying the three alternative activating conditions remain operationally distinguishable.
candidates.observed: The exact closed FCSTM and source inventory model the activation edge DetectingState->junction1 (transition:line:22 / tr_0002) with a single merged trigger 'Frontend_Collision_or_Rear_end_Collision_or_Collision_with_Pedestrian_detected' and no guard; there is no separate event or guard per condition, so the three named alternative conditions are not distinguishable at the model level.
candidates.reason: NL explicitly treats frontend collision, rear-end collision, and pedestrian collision as three separate detection conditions triggering the same activation, and the guard_disjointness property from NL-CONTRACT-NL2-TRIGGERSET-1 requires these alternatives to remain distinguishable; the closed model exposes exactly one trigger with no distinguishing guard, which is the precise semantic gap this contract targets.
candidates.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The single merged event name textually preserves all three conditions in its label, and a downstream event producer might dispatch three semantically distinct event instances that happen to share this one declared FCSTM event identity; if so the merge is only a naming/declaration convenience and does not itself prove indistinguishability at runtime.
candidates.title: Three named detection conditions collapsed into one indistinguishable activation trigger

candidates.basis: fcstm_model.text region comment block ([PlantUML concurrent region 0] states=-; transitions=-; region1 states=BrakeControlState,junction2; region2 states=SteeringControlState,junction3; region3 states=SensorControlState,junction4,InitialState); inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING for junction2/junction3/InitialState; reference_inspection_facts W_DEADLOCK_LEAF x3.
candidates.expected: The four declared concurrent regions of ActiveState must each structurally support concurrent, ongoing activation of a distinct collision-avoidance control (e.g., braking, steering, sensor control).
candidates.observed: The exact closed FCSTM/source structure declares 4 concurrent regions under ActiveState: region 0 has no member states at all (states=-; transitions=-), while regions 1-3 each terminate at a leaf junction state (junction2, junction3, InitialState respectively) with zero outgoing transitions per inspection_equivalent_facts and reference_inspection_facts (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING / W_DEADLOCK_LEAF). One region is structurally empty and the other three dead-end, so none of the four regions structurally realizes ongoing concurrent control activation.
candidates.reason: NL3 requires the orthogonal region structure itself to support ongoing concurrent activation of distinct controls; the exact declared region topology (one empty region, three dead-end regions) is a structural fact directly bearing on this obligation independent of any single transition/state check.
candidates.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: PlantUML concurrent separators create region boundaries by convention even when a region has no states, and a leaf junction with no outgoing edge may represent a terminal 'settled' control state rather than a structural region-support defect; the NL wording is high-level and may only require declared parallel regions to exist, which they structurally do.
candidates.title: Orthogonal regions of ActiveState do not sustain concurrent operation of distinct collision-avoidance controls

response.reason: This lens audits contract completeness/structure and contrastive consistency across author source and closed FCSTM for case 0027. Key findings: (1) NL1 cardinality (3 regions) requires a cardinality_binding row, not a candidate; the exact source/FCSTM structure shows ActiveState declares 4 concurrent regions (region 0 empty, region1=Brake/junction2, region2=Steering/junction3, region3=Sensor/junction4/InitialState), which is a mismatch worth flagging via the binding for downstream frontier comparison. (2) NL2 initial_entry: owner=root/enclosing scope, target=collision-avoidance sub-machine (ActiveState). The exact source/model shows [*] -> DetectingState -> junction1 -> ActiveState triggered by the named event; ActiveState is reached only via this one edge, and it is the sole activation path, satisfying the owner-local entry obligation, so no candidate is emitted for NL2 itself. (3) NL2 trigger-set/guard_disjointness: the sub-machine activation edge (DetectingState->junction1) carries exactly one merged event trigger representing all three named detection conditions, with no distinguishing guard among them; because the source combines three semantically distinct alternatives into one indistinguishable trigger, this is a real guard_disjointness/W1 candidate. (4) NL3 containment: ActiveState's four orthogonal regions are structurally contained within ActiveState per the FCSTM model text (regions declared inside ActiveState), so containment is satisfied structurally; however (5) NL3 region_structure and state_action reveal a structural defect: three of the four regions (region1/2/3) end in leaf junction states (junction2, junction3, InitialState) with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING / W_DEADLOCK_LEAF diagnostics), and region 0 has no member states at all (empty region), which contradicts the NL3 obligation that orthogonal regions sustain concurrent, ongoing operation of distinct collision-avoidance controls. This routes to a derived initial_entry-adjacent structural gap (region 0 has no default entry/target — no BrakeControlState-equivalent state at all) and to the existing region_structure/state_action contracts as W1 candidates using deterministic leaf/diagnostic facts. I use inspection_equivalent_facts, exact_source_inventory, and fcstm_model.text (concurrent region comments) as the exact source of the region count and topology.

The complete closed-model inventory and deterministic deadlock-frontier facts show all three concurrent regions reach a leaf with no outgoing transition, which is a reachable non-final no-continuation fact matching the V1(initial_scope) frontier pattern, even though V1 cannot fully express the 'concurrent sustained operation across regions' semantics, hence predicate_id is retained as V1 with W1-level scholarly support per the routing discipline for deadlock-frontier facts feeding a progress obligation.

issues.expected: Three distinguishable alternative activating conditions (frontend collision, rear-end collision, pedestrian collision) should each independently and distinguishably trigger activation of the collision-avoidance sub-machine, e.g. via separate events/guards or a disjoint condition structure.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM defines exactly one event, 'Frontend_Collision_or_Rear_end_Collision_or_Collision_with_Pedestrian_detected', consumed by a single transition DetectingState->junction1 with no guard and no per-condition distinction; the exact_source_inventory likewise records only one combined event string on tr_0002. The three named conditions are therefore operationally indistinguishable under this single trigger with no guard differentiation.
issues.reason: NL2's trigger-set contract explicitly requires the three named detection conditions to remain distinguishable activating alternatives; the closed model and source inventory both show only one combined event string with no guard on the sole activation transition, so the three alternatives cannot be operationally distinguished from one another, precisely matching the guard_disjointness violation direction (wrong_guard) even though no frozen predicate can express this semantic property.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL's own phrasing already coordinates the three detection conditions with 'or', so a single combined trigger event may faithfully represent one composite activation condition rather than three independently guarded alternatives that must be kept operationally distinguishable; no frozen predicate directly expresses guard/trigger disjointness, so this remains predicate-null and its materiality depends on whether NL truly intends three separately distinguishable alternatives.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, termination, and region structure. The FCSTM shows DetectingState -> junction1 -> ActiveState is exactly one edge with initial pseudo-state entries into three parallel branches inside ActiveState (BrakeControlState/junction2, SteeringControlState/junction3, SensorControlState/junction4/InitialState). All three branches terminate at reachable leaves with zero outgoing transitions (junction2, junction3, InitialState), confirmed by inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and verify_facts deadlock checks (status=refuted, meaning the deadlock property could not be proved absent, i.e. these are genuine dead ends). NL3's state_action contract requires the active mode's concurrent regions to sustain ongoing concurrent operation ("continuously allow simultaneous activation... onward operating behavior across regions must be sustained rather than blocked"); this is an explicit progress/continuation obligation, and the three parallel branches each dead-end at a leaf with no outgoing transition, which is a direct violation of that sustained-operation obligation. This routes to V1(initial_scope) using the three leaf refs as supporting evidence. NL2's initial_entry contract's owner (root/enclosing scope) -> DetectingState edge exists and reaches DetectingState; the sub-machine activation edge (DetectingState->junction1->ActiveState) is also present and triggered by the single combined event, so the owner-local entry into ActiveState is satisfied structurally; no candidate is emitted for initial_entry since the edge exists and reaches the correct target with the trigger. Event-consumer coverage for the sole event is declared and reachable (DetectingState consumes it), satisfying NL2's activation trigger existence, but NL2 additionally requires the trigger set to represent three distinguishable named conditions; the FCSTM collapses all three into one combined event/trigger string on a single transition, so the alternatives are not independently distinguishable -- this supports NL-CONTRACT-NL2-TRIGGERSET-1's guard_disjointness claim (predicate-null W1) since all three conditions map to the same single trigger with no guard differentiation. Region structure (NL3-REGIONSTRUCTURE-1) is satisfied: the FCSTM text explicitly declares 3 concurrent PlantUML regions with concurrent activation semantics inside ActiveState, so no candidate needed there. Containment (NL3-CONTAINMENT-1) is also satisfied since regions are declared as children/regions of ActiveState. Cardinality binding for NL1 is provided separately; the state_action dead-end issue is the primary behavioral consequence finding.

stage_receipts.reason: Extracted atomic obligations: NL1 gives an explicit three-region cardinality requirement over concurrent orthogonal regions of the diagram/sub-machine. NL2 establishes an activation/initial-entry obligation into the collision-avoidance sub-machine triggered by three alternative detection events, plus a distinguishability obligation among those alternative triggers. NL3 splits into three independent obligations from one sentence: containment of the orthogonal regions within the active collision-avoidance mode, the orthogonal/concurrent region-structure property itself, and a continuous operating state_action obligation that concurrent activation of distinct controls must be sustained while the mode is active. No transition_groups were warranted because no explicit named source-to-named-target endpoint relation with alternative destinations is stated; NL2's alternatives are detection triggers for one activation/entry, not distinct transition targets, so they are captured via initial_entry binding hints and a guard_disjointness contract rather than a transition_groups structure.
